note: Single source of truth for risk signals, shared by the tracer's live check, the case catalog's lure tags, and (later) the agentic job-cleaner skill. Weights are additive evidence points; silence adds nothing.

signals.label: Website domain registered less than 6 months ago
signals.why: Scam operations spin up fresh domains and abandon them once reported.

signals.label: Website domain registered less than 2 years ago
signals.why: Young domain; weak signal on its own, stronger when the company claims a long history.

signals.label: Recruiter uses a free email provider
signals.why: Legitimate employers almost always recruit from a company domain.

signals.label: Recruiter email domain differs from the company website
signals.why: Common impersonation pattern: a real company's name with a look-alike or unrelated email domain.

signals.label: Interview or contact only via Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal or similar
signals.why: Moves the conversation off platforms that keep records or moderate.

signals.label: Asks the candidate to pay (training, equipment, visa, placement, deposit)
signals.why: Legitimate employers do not charge applicants. Recruitment fees are a core forced-labour indicator (ILO).

signals.label: Requests passport, ID, SSN or bank details before an interview
signals.why: Identity theft risk; document retention is a trafficking control tactic.

signals.label: Pay far above market for little experience
signals.why: Bait pay is the most common lure in both scam and trafficking recruitment.

signals.label: "No experience needed" combined with urgency or high pay
signals.why: Broad-funnel lure.

signals.label: Pressure to accept or travel within hours or days
signals.why: Urgency prevents the candidate from checking the offer.

signals.label: Employer arranges and controls travel and housing
signals.why: Control of movement and lodging is a trafficking indicator (Polaris, UNODC), especially abroad.

signals.label: Work location is vague or disclosed only on arrival
signals.why: Prevents the candidate or family from knowing where they will be.

signals.label: Overseas role in a region with documented scam-compound recruitment
signals.why: UNODC and OHCHR document forced scam work in parts of Myanmar, Cambodia and Laos, often recruited via Thailand, Malaysia or Dubai.

signals.label: Role type frequently used as a lure (modeling, hostess, "customer service" abroad, crypto/data entry)
signals.why: Low-verification roles are easy to fabricate.

signals.label: Job involves receiving or forwarding money, gift cards or crypto
signals.why: Money-mule and check-cashing scams.

signals.label: Interview scheduled at an unusual hour for the stated location
signals.why: Suggests the recruiter operates from a different country than claimed.

signals.label: Matches an entity, former name or alias in the documented case catalog
signals.why: The case record lists the enforcement action or report and its sources.

signals.label: Matched through a former name, DBA or alias
signals.why: Re-registering under a new name is a common way to shed complaints and enforcement history.

signals.label: Employer keeps or will hold passports or ID documents
signals.why: Retention of identity documents is one of the ILO forced-labour indicators.

signals.label: Recruitment costs become a debt repaid from wages
signals.why: Debt bondage is one of the ILO forced-labour indicators.

signals.label: Visa type does not match the work, or sponsorship is promised without a certified employer
signals.why: Tourist or student visas for work make the worker deportable and dependent.

signals.label: Recruiter's email domain has no mail server (MX) record
signals.why: The domain cannot receive email normally, a sign of a throwaway or spoofed address.

signals.label: First TLS certificate for the domain issued less than 6 months ago
signals.why: Confirms a recently stood-up website even where registration dates are hidden.

signals.label: No Wayback Machine history for the website
signals.why: Weak on its own; strong when the company claims years of operation.

signals.label: Registry lists the entity as delinquent, dissolved or inactive
signals.why: An entity not in good standing should not be hiring.

signals.label: Registered entity formed less than 12 months ago
signals.why: New entities are common in re-registration after complaints.

signals.label: Entity has previous legal names on record
signals.why: Name changes are usually benign; they matter when an earlier name is linked to reports or enforcement.

tiers.label: Little evidence found
tiers.advice: The checks that ran found little. That is not a clearance: see coverage, and verify the recruiter through the company's official website or phone line before sharing documents or travelling.

tiers.label: Caution
tiers.advice: Several weak signals. Verify independently before sharing documents or accepting travel.

tiers.label: High risk
tiers.advice: Strong scam or exploitation indicators. Do not pay, send ID, or travel. Consider reporting.
